resolution.note: Root cause: a task id anywhere in the checkout path (tmpdir inside a lane worktree) was read as the session identity by scope.worker, edit-standards and the compaction identifier index. Proved by test/hook/scope.test.ts and test/claude/identifier-index.test.ts regressions, and the stop and context-restart tests passing with TMPDIR inside a lane worktree and KRN_TASK/KRN_LANE/KRN_SESSION_CLASS set.

title: Hook tests build their own task identity, so a lane's base run stays green
body:
Observed 2026-11-19: `krn lane run --task t-wfc37b4` and `--task t-kkbqvqy` both stopped with "the base suite is red" before any session started. The base run inside the lane worktree failed two tests that pass on main: test/hook/stop.test.ts:688 ('a lane session with slug fix-x ... one with no identity is refused' got "no commit" instead of /names no task/) and test/claude/context-restart.test.ts:19 (additionalContext gained a '- Tasks: t-wfc37b4' line before '- Paths:'). The lane's own task identity (env such as KRN_TASK/KRN_LANE/KRN_SESSION_CLASS, or the worktree branch name) leaks into the fixtures, so every task lane is refused while these tests run in a lane worktree. Logs: .krn/worktrees/t-wfc37b4/.krn/tmp/base-run.log.
Principle: a test fixture builds its whole identity (env and git) itself; nothing from the session running the suite reaches the code under test.
Files: test/hook/stop.test.ts, test/claude/context-restart.test.ts (and the source that reads the leaked identity, if the leak is in the code rather than the fixture)
Outcome: both tests pass when the suite runs with KRN_TASK=t-zzzzzzz KRN_LANE=t-zzzzzzz KRN_SESSION_CLASS=lane in the environment and from a checkout on a branch named like a task id; a regression test (or the existing ones under that env) proves it.
Proof: `KRN_TASK=t-zzzzzzz KRN_LANE=t-zzzzzzz KRN_SESSION_CLASS=lane node --test test/hook/stop.test.ts test/claude/context-restart.test.ts` prints pass.
